`root>low` creates a new stacking context because it is positioned (`position: absolute`) and has a `z-index` of 1. As a result, its child `root>low>inner` is scoped within that context, and its high `z-index` of 999 only applies relative to other elements inside `root>low`. Since `root>high` is a sibling of `root>low` with a higher `z-index` (2 vs 1), it is rendered above `root>low` and all of its descendants in the overlapping region.

ANSWER: root>high
